notes: This minor release requires Bifrost 0.15.2 or later, up from 0.15.1, and depends exactly on bifrost.public.packs 0.13.0. Migration: Bifrost 0.15.1 and earlier reject the whole catalog of this release, because bifrost.javascript-codeql-quality declares an identifier typo table and bifrost.rust-codeql-quality uses a policy completion rule that those engines do not read; upgrade to Bifrost 0.15.2, or stay on rules 0.13.0. Every locked policy identity verifies on the released Bifrost 0.15.2, whose capability names are the same as 0.15.1's. New policy: bifrost.java-codeql-quality.missing-override-annotation (CodeQL java/missing-override-annotation parity, severity warning) in bifrost.java-codeql-quality 0.2.0 (#120). It reports a method that overrides a superclass or interface method without @Override; same-arity overloads are no longer treated as overrides on Bifrost 0.15.2 (bifrost-dev#9900). An override of a JDK method whose ancestor Bifrost has not read (such as Runnable.run, Comparable.compareTo or Object.toString) is not reported, and the run is inconclusive rather than clean (bifrost-dev#7027). Changed: bifrost.javascript-codeql-quality 0.2.0 ships an Apache-2.0 identifier typo table built from the Apache OpenOffice en-US AutoCorrect list and a Brokk-authored supplement, and bifrost.javascript-codeql-quality.misspelled-identifier (severity note) now reports only identifiers in that table, as possible findings, instead of leaving every run inconclusive (#332, bifrost-dev#10386). Changed: bifrost.rust-codeql-quality 0.2.0 makes bifrost.rust-codeql-quality.ctor-initialization report its run as inconclusive when the caller search reaches its depth bound, where it previously reported complete and could silently miss a call deeper than the bound (#333, bifrost-dev#10088). New catalogs, no policy: bifrost.java-codeql-security 0.1.0 holds 26 CodeQL-generated Java and Servlet source and sink catalogs (MIT, derived from github/codeql ae741615f3e178ce61289a651790dc67fcc18e19) (#143). It registers no policy and enables nothing; the path-injection policy that will use it is not in this release. All other policies, IDs and required capabilities are unchanged from rules 0.13.0. This release does not qualify the full policy set or imply complete analysis.
